 Hall Reflects On Newcastle United’s “Weird” Season
 Caroline Dowse 
 Lewis Hall has remarked on what he calls a “weird” season for Newcastle United .
 Newcastle have had a patchy start to the season. They have lost four times in the Premier League and have been knocked out of the Carabao Cup by Everton .
 Hall was speaking after England’s game against Croatia at Wembley last night, which the Three Lions won 2-1. The win means that England have qualified for the Nations League quarterfinals.
 Newcastle Will Get “Better and Better”
 22-year-old Hall said that it has been a “weird” season for Newcastle so far. They have been inconsistent, looking good in games against Liverpool and Tottenham Hotspur , then falling apart against Leeds United and Coventry City . The team have looked devoid of ideas and identity at times.
 Last weekend’s draw with Fulham will have calmed a few nerves, but the full-back admitted that things have been “difficult” for a mostly young, inexperienced team, but is confident that they will improve.
 “It has been a weird season. We have shown in spells what a great team we can be. We have a young squad, but it’s only going to get better and better.
 “I think it’s difficult, the situation that we are in at the minute, but we are working hard in training and really looking forward to what’s coming up.”
 He played alongside teammate and club captain Dan Burn against Croatia, and also linked up with former teammates Anthony Gordon and Elliot Anderson, an experience he described as being like a “Newcastle reunion”.
 “It was great to be alongside Dan Burn, and having Anthony Gordon on the left with Elliot Anderson in midfield – it was like a Newcastle reunion.
 “It was nice to be part of that. I am really happy for Dan Burn, who is a really experienced player in his own right. I know how much it means to him to play for England. To share the pitch with him again was special.”
 Hall is determined to make the left-back spot his own, but knows that he faces competition from Nico O’Reilly and Djed Spence. Both players were picked ahead of Hall for Thomas Tuchel’s World Cup squad, and Hall’s omission baffled many people. But Hall is up for the challenge.
 “I just focus on myself and do what I can do and my own performances on the pitch. There is a really strong competition and we’ve seen the performances of Djed Spence and Nico O’Reilly at the World Cup.
 “I know it is tough competition but every opportunity I get out there, especially like last night, I am looking to take it and make sure it counts.”

 Kane Is “Really Inspirational”
 It was a special night for England captain Harry Kane, who earned his 126th cap, making him the most-capped player in England’s history.
 Morgan Rogers scored England’s first goal in the 24th minute after a good England move, but Croatia pulled one back in the 59th minute after a mix-up in the England defence. But Kane was not to be denied, getting his 92nd England goal with a penalty in the 64th minute after a foul on Jarell Quansah.
 Hall described Kane as “really inspirational”, and praised the 33-year-old’s “hard work and dedication”.
 "It was an honour to share a night like this with him!" ❤️

 “He is really inspirational, not just his footballing ability but how he is as a person. The hard work and dedication that we see every day.
 “I always learn from every game I play. Every training session too. I never take it for granted; it is a privilege to be playing not just for England, but with some of the best players in the world.”
 England’s final game of this international break is against Spain on Sunday at the Riyadh Air Metropolitano stadium in Madrid. The result will decide which team tops the group.
 Caroline Dowse
 Caroline is the Newcastle United writer for Vital Football. She has a BA in English with Creative Writing from University Centre Peterborough, and a year's sports writing experience.
